title: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Custom Value Guide: Yearly Prices
description: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Custom values by year, from 1950s Black Beauties to 1979, with original-part considerations and photos from my guitar archive.
h1: Vintage Gibson Les Paul Custom Value Guide
alt: Black 1958 Les Paul Custom body with three covered pickups, a Bigsby vibrato and visible finish wear

faqs.q: What Is A Vintage Gibson Les Paul Custom Worth?
faqs.a: The site's clean-original reference for 1968 to 1969 Customs is $12,000 to $18,000. Standard two-pickup 1975 to 1979 Customs have a published clean-condition reference of $5,000 to $6,500. Original 1950s guitars use separate pickup-based bands. The annual table explains the source and condition assumed.

faqs.q: Does Every Year Have A Separate Price?
faqs.a: Every covered production year has a row, but neighboring years can share an era reference. Repeated figures don't claim an independent same-year transaction sample. The model's configuration and condition are still needed for a closer appraisal.

faqs.q: Why Are There No Carved-Body Custom Rows For 1961 To 1967?
faqs.a: The site's family identification guide ends the original carved-body run in 1960 and records its return in 1968. SG-shaped Customs belong to a different body family. An unusual transitional example needs individual identification rather than an assumed carved-body price.

faqs.q: Does A Three-Pickup Custom Always Cost More?
faqs.a: No fixed premium applies to every year and condition. I check whether the arrangement is factory original, whether the pickups remain original and which era is being compared. A later conversion doesn't inherit the value of an original factory configuration.

faqs.q: Is A Refretted Custom Still All Original?
faqs.a: A quality refret preserves the all-original classification of an otherwise original guitar under this site's grading approach. It removes museum-quality status. Neck reshaping, a replaced fingerboard and structural repairs are separate alterations.

faqs.q: Can I Use An Asking Price As A Completed Sale?
faqs.a: No. An asking price is a seller's request. I use the transaction-history final price for completed Reverb comparisons and then review the listing's year, parts and condition. A sold label alone doesn't establish the amount paid.

faqs.q: Should I Polish Or Replace Parts Before An Appraisal?
faqs.a: Photograph the guitar as it is first. Keep any removed original parts and known repair records with it. I don't need you to change hardware, disturb wiring or authorize cosmetic work before an initial appraisal.
